final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition of Credit Suisse backed by CHF 50 billion SNB liquidity facility and CHF 15 billion Federal Council loss guarantee, with explicit capital hierarchy (equity exhausted at 11bn, AT1 absorbs next 5.5bn, government covers remainder to 15bn cap). All parties committed to 23:00 public announcement with CS CEO authorized to call top clients immediately.
minority_objections: AT1 rep initially objected that equity-first language was ambiguous without hard numbers
Wealth client worried unnamed liquidity commitment would signal desperation rather than strength
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs SNB on whether to name CHF 50bn publicly (FC initially resisted, SNB demanded it)
AT1 rep vs FINMA on whether AT1 write-down risk was adequately disclosed in guarantee language
UBS CEO vs Federal Council on timing of legal guarantees (UBS demanded 22:30 delivery as signature condition)
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to name CHF 50bn liquidity publicly despite initial resistance to avoid signaling desperation
FINMA rewrote guarantee text mid-meeting to reflect CS equity already at 11bn (negative after 14bn losses), making AT1 write-down explicit
SNB agreed to make AT1 instruments eligible collateral for emergency facility effective immediately
Federal Council capped loss exposure at CHF 15bn hard stop with automatic UBS renegotiation trigger above that
CS CEO authorized to call top twenty wealth clients immediately after 22:50 text publication to stop weekend deposit flight
red_lines: Federal Council: CHF 15bn loss cap absolute ceiling, no open-ended guarantee or blank check
UBS CEO: acquisition contingent on written government guarantees delivered by 22:30, would walk without them
SNB: emergency liquidity requires Federal Council public commitment, would not backstop unknowns beyond 15bn
AT1 rep: demanded explicit numerical loss hierarchy in writing or threatened litigation would kill rescue
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Litigation risk from AT1 holders was raised repeatedly but never resulted in concrete mitigation beyond disclosure language
Operational risk that Monday facility draws would be visible and misread as distress signal was addressed only in final rounds
Contagion risk to broader Swiss banking system was never discussed
Political backlash risk from taxpayer exposure was acknowledged but not deeply explored
downstream_risk_variables: Whether CS top-twenty client calls tonight actually stop weekend deposit flight
Whether markets read Monday AT1 write-down as capped/expected vs contagion signal despite 06:00 SNB statement
Whether CHF 15bn loss cap proves sufficient or triggers UBS renegotiation clause
Whether visible facility draws Tuesday create renewed panic despite published framework
Whether AT1 holders litigate despite explicit hierarchy disclosure
uncertainty_notes: The room achieved legal and operational consensus but left three critical uncertainties unresolved: (1) whether immediate client outreach actually stops the weekend run or merely slows it, (2) whether Monday market open reads the AT1 write-down as controlled loss absorption or contagion trigger despite messaging, and (3) whether the CHF 15bn cap proves adequate or forces Monday renegotiation. The rescue structure is legally defensible but operationally untested under live market conditions.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: FINMA R1 demanded solvency package modeling because 'liquidity alone fails'; Federal Council R2 rejected liquidity-only as insufficient, required loss protection; entire rescue pivoted from liquidity to acquisition structure
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became binding decision by R3; Federal Council R4 locked acquisition language in 23:00 release as first substantive sentence; UBS CEO signature by R7 contingent on guarantees drove final structure
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 50bn SNB liquidity and CHF 15bn Federal Council loss guarantee became non-negotiable conditions for UBS signature; government backstop explicitly required in writing before UBS would commit; shaped every number and timeline
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client R1 warned confidence below 12 triggers freefall; CS CEO R2 stated clients deciding to pull cash this weekend; R10 CS CEO authorized to call top-twenty clients immediately to stop weekend run; drove urgency of 23:00 announcement
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down became explicit in rescue structure after FINMA R7 rewrite acknowledging equity exhausted; 5.5bn AT1 loss layer locked into guarantee text; AT1 collateral eligibility for facility became binding term; drove capital hierarchy negotiations
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 rep R2-R6 repeatedly demanded explicit loss hierarchy in writing; FINMA rewrote guarantee mid-meeting to clarify equity-then-AT1 sequence; but conflict was resolved through disclosure rather than changing who bears losses
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep R2 warned litigation would 'kill rescue faster than liquidity gap'; R6 warned courts would challenge hierarchy; R9 demanded explicit AT1 cap number; acknowledged throughout but only addressed via disclosure language, not structural change
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: 22:00 SNB model deadline, 22:30 guarantee delivery deadline, 22:50 text publication, 23:00 public release all became binding constraints; UBS threatened to walk if 22:30 missed; drove every decision timeline and forced concessions
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Discussed extensively (Monday panic, market open confidence, facility draw visibility) but did not force structural changes to the deal—addressed through messaging strategy (06:00 SNB statement, client calls) rather than altering rescue terms
